_readme: 'bearing_receptors' entries carry a fixed bearing (and distance, where the ES states one) taken directly from the ES text - used only where no verified coordinate exists yet. 'latlon_receptors' entries carry a verified lat/lon (from Google Maps satellite imagery) - the script computes exact bearing AND straight-line distance from the stack automatically. Prefer latlon_receptors wherever you have a real coordinate; it's more precise than the ES's rounded 8-point compass directions (see discrepancy notes below).

stack.name: AWRP main EfW stack
stack.source: User-verified via Google Maps satellite imagery - base of stack, confirmed 2026-09-10.

_bearing_receptors_note: These are the ES Ch.10 Table 10.19 receptors. 'bearing_deg' and 'distance_m' are the figures the ES states, kept for provenance and for comparison. 'verified_lat'/'verified_lon' are real coordinates taken from Google Maps satellite imagery on 2026-10-12; when present the script uses them for bearing and distance instead of the ES figures, so the ES's rounded 8-point compass directions no longer drive the downwind check for these points. An entry with no verified coordinate falls back to the ES bearing/distance.

_discrepancy_notes.Arkendale: ES Ch.10 Table 10.19 states 270deg/1750m ('west'). The verified coordinate (outside the church) computes to 304deg/2073m - closer to Ch.12's looser text description ('north-west'). The 2011 table figure appears rounded to the nearest 8-point compass direction.
_discrepancy_notes.Flaxby_resolved: An earlier version of this file had Flaxby's coordinate wrong (it was actually the Bay Horse Inn, which is in Green Hammerton, not Flaxby) - that produced a bearing of 120deg/SE which contradicted the ES's 'south-west'. Corrected 2026-09-10: Flaxby now points to York Road/Shortsill Lane, which computes to 207deg/2.21km - consistent with the ES's 'south-west' description. Green Hammerton has been added as its own entry using the coordinate that was mistakenly applied to Flaxby before.
